title: Crimson Reef Logistics pilot kickoff - raw call notes
content:
Call: Crimson Reef Logistics (CRL) - kickoff with platform + infra + product
Date: 2024-11-05 
Attendees: Samir Patel (CTO), Lena Ortiz (SRE lead), Alex Mercer (product), Jordan Kim (RSE), Priya Nair (solutions) 

High level ask (customer speak):
- Real-time natural language assistant for freight ops: intake free-text manifests, summarize exceptions, suggest reroutes, and surface contracts/clause matches.
- Must run in their EU-only environment; cannot route any PII outside customer VPC.
- SLA: 99th percentile inference latency <= 150ms for single-turn summaries at median token sizes; throughput baseline 40 QPS with bursts to 120 QPS during morning window.
- Cost sensitivity: prefer quantized open models but want Redwood reliability features (rollouts, fallbacks).

Notes / clarifications from call: (rough)
- Data residency is hard requirement (GDPR + internal policy). They will not accept hosted multi-tenant API for PII endpoints.
- Two deployment lanes: (A) private VPC (control plane managed) for prod; (B) Dedicated reserved pool for non-PII internal tooling during evaluation.
- Key management: must use customer's Azure Key Vault + HSM-backed wrapping. Need KMS integration proof-of-concept.
- Context length: average inbound manifests ~350 tokens, but edge-case manifests can be 1.8k-2.4k tokens (lots of line items). Suggest KV/prefix caching or dynamic truncation strategies.
- Compose pipeline: embedding-based retrieval (hourly index refresh) -> candidate extraction -> reranker -> final summary generation. Reranker must be fast (p95 < 60ms).

Technical constraints / gotchas flagged by CRL: 
- Network: some regional edge nodes (Spain, Poland) have flaky throughput; they want regional routing and fallback to central EU pool.
- Token limits: manifests sometimes include scanned OCR noise; need normalization heuristics to avoid explosion.
- Audit: full request/response audit logs retained for 1 year, but logs must be stored in their S3 bucket behind VPC endpoint. Need guidance on log export from Redwood Private.
- Retry/fallback policy: if quantized model times out, failover to smaller model increases latency — they prefer graceful degrade to short summary + link to full doc rather than silent failure.

Model/infra recommendations (Rough RSE thinking):
- Start: redwood-7b-q4f (quantized) in Private deployment with Dedicated burst pool for morning peaks. 7b should hit cost targets and latency with tuning.
- Use KV cache for repeated manifest prefixes + continuous batching tuned to 12-16 tokens per request to hit throughput while keeping p99 low.
- Reranker: run lightweight model (distil-rranker) on CPU instance colocated with GPU pool to keep <60ms p95. Evaluate candidate counts (k=8 default).
- Indexing: embeddings (hourly) stored in FAISS on customer infra; Redwood should be able to call into repo or run in their VPC. Clarify whether embeddings compute needs to be in Private plane or can be Dedicated.

Open questions (need to follow up):
- Q1: Can CRL accept model artefacts being downloaded from our catalogue into their air-gapped network? If not, need signed-package workflow. (Ticket INF-5842)
- Q2: Exact retention/format for audit logs - JSONL vs gzipped protobuf? Who manages lifecycle? (Action: Lena to confirm)
- Q3: Peak concurrency profile — they gave rough morning spike windows but need per-minute distribution to right-size autoscale. (Action: Alex to share 2-week traffic export)

Immediate action items / next steps (owners + due dates):
- Jordan: Put together two-runway deployment proposal (Private prod + Dedicated eval) with cost delta estimate. Due 2024-11-12.
- Priya: Draft security checklist for KMS/HSM integration and required customer artifacts for onboarding. Due 2024-11-08.
- Priya + Marta: Prepare short demo script showing graceful fallback and reranker speed tradeoffs (include token lengths). Demo request by 2024-11-15.
- Lena (CRL): Share traffic export + sample manifests (anonymized) by 2024-11-09.
- Samir (CRL): Confirm legal signoff timeline for 1-year audit retention by 2024-11-20.

Short-term experiment ideas (cheap, demoable):
- Run embedding-only job in their VPC using a small Dedicated pool; show retrieval latency & freshness with hourly updates.
- Simulate OCR-heavy manifests to test normalization heuristics + truncation fallback; measure quality delta.
- Canary: deploy reranker CPU instance and test p95 across 1k samples.

Risks & mitigation notes: 
- Risk: Edge packet loss + cross-region routing causes increased tail latency -> Mitigation: use smart routing + keep cold-standby VM pool in central EU for failover.
- Risk: Large manifests blow up token costs -> Mitigation: aggressive preprocessing (strip low-value lines), summarization-first step to reduce tokens before final generation.
- Risk: Customer refuses to accept third-party S3 export -> Mitigation: implement log export to their S3 via private link from Private control plane.

Random misc: 
- Customer liked the idea of model pinning per route and per-environment; want explicit UI/CLI to lock a rollout. We'll flag product ask to console team.
- They asked about function-calling for structured outputs (manifest -> JSON). Recommend enabling function schemas for final stage; we'll include a small sample schema in next demo.

References / links captured in call: 
- Jira INF-5842 (model artefact delivery)
- Confluence draft: Crimson Reef pilot spec (internal)
- GitHub PR 812 (infra: vpc-log-export helpers)

Notes to self: 
- Don't promise full air-gap packaging without legal+infra signoff.
- Keep reranker latency as marketing differentiator — measure p95 not mean.
- Follow up with product-hosted-api team on whether there is any quick checkbox for EU-data-only hosted endpoints (they said no, but confirm).

End of raw notes — these will be refined into a short internal kickoff doc once traffic artifacts arrive.

-- Jordan
